_about: Site-specific interpretive text for notebook 03's summary.json (Sweihan). Every string is a Python format template filled from this run's numbers (vs, nd, ph, s30, l30, ws, qc, P, n_dunes, pct_below, tt: see the seih_al_hama file). Written after looking at this site's notebook 02 and 03 results; ranges quoted literally (heights, body speeds) are from the 2026-11-15 run.

published.reference: No published dune-migration rate for Sweihan (Phase 1b literature search, docs/research/aoi-sweihan-liwa.md section 5)
published.our_value: {vs[detected_speed_median_myr]:.2f} m/yr median (10-90 %: {vs[detected_speed_p10_p90_myr][0]:.2f}-{vs[detected_speed_p10_p90_myr][1]:.2f}) toward {ph[field_median_heading_deg]:.0f} deg, 2013-2025, windows with detected motion
published.note: No comparison is possible. The nearest local number, the Seih Al Hama thesis value '3.32 m', has no stated time base and is from a different field 45 km away, so it is not used. The Landsat 7 epochs (2000, 2001) give the same speed over 2000-2025 as 2013-2025, which is the only long-term check available.

wind_agreement_note: mean |heading - RDD| over detected windows, RDD {ws[RDD_deg]} deg (MERRA-2 2000-2024). The regime is bimodal (RDP/DP {ws[RDP_DP]}), but here the dunes follow the resultant: the field-median heading {ph[field_median_heading_deg]} deg is {ph[field_heading_minus_RDD_deg]} deg from RDD, {ph[field_heading_minus_modes_deg][0]} deg from the strongest (north-westerly) mode and {ph[field_heading_minus_modes_deg][1]} deg from the opposing one; per-window median difference {ph[per_window_abs_heading_minus_RDD_median_deg]} deg.
second_dataset_note: The independent Sentinel-2 check agrees on direction (field headings {s30[heading_difference_deg]} deg apart) but gives about half the speed ({s30[field_median_speed_hls_myr]} vs {s30[field_median_speed_landsat_myr]} m/yr) and agrees only weakly window by window (r {s30[corr_E]}/{s30[corr_N]}); at 30 m its detection limit ({s30[hls_detection_limit_median_myr]} m/yr) is close to most measured speeds. Where Landsat speeds exceed twice the detection limit ({s30[windows_where_landsat_speed_gt_2x_detection_limit][n]} windows) headings differ by a median {s30[windows_where_landsat_speed_gt_2x_detection_limit][median_heading_diff_deg]} deg. HLS L30 agrees better (heading within {l30[heading_difference_deg]} deg, speed {l30[field_median_speed_hls_myr]} vs {l30[field_median_speed_landsat_myr]} m/yr, r {l30[corr_E]}/{l30[corr_N]}) but uses the same Landsat instruments, so it only shows the result survives a different band, resolution and processing.
limits: Detected dune windows move a median {vs[detected_speed_median_myr]:.2f} m/yr (10-90 %: {vs[detected_speed_p10_p90_myr][0]:.2f}-{vs[detected_speed_p10_p90_myr][1]:.2f}, max {vs[detected_speed_range_myr][1]:.2f}), i.e. roughly 15-45 m in 25 years; {pct_below:.0f} % of valid dune windows move below the detection limit (median {nd[detection_limit_median_myr]:.2f} m/yr) and have no measured direction.

Reach years forecast the migration of dune forms (slip-face advance), not wind-blown sand crossing a road, which happens wherever a road borders loose sand, whatever the dunes do (see borders_free_sand in targets.geojson).
At about 1 m/yr one 15 m pixel is about 15 years of motion, so reach years for targets near the sand carry an edge uncertainty of +-7.5 m plus the outline uncertainty of the target.
Most targets are not reached by {P[projection_end]}; targets flagged 'sand at edge now' already have migrating sand within that edge uncertainty.
The projection is advection along the measured 2013-2025 motion, assuming those conditions continue; it does not model dune deformation, merging, splitting or growth.
Vegetation, windbreaks, sand fences, levelling, construction and climate change alter the outcome.

Motion is measured in 480 m windows: it is the motion of the small dunes (spacing ~{qc[linearity_aliasing][dune_spacing_25pct_variance_below_m]}-{qc[linearity_aliasing][dune_spacing_spectral_peak_m]} m) and sand sheets inside, not of the large ridges they ride on; those ridge bodies, tracked separately at 960 m scale, move about 0.2-0.3 m/yr (detected for {qc[draa_bodies][n_detected]} of {qc[draa_bodies][n_valid]} trackable bodies).

Only {n_dunes} large dunes (13-45 m high) are outlined, from NASADEM (February 2000) shifted to 2025; the small dunes that carry most of the motion are represented by the velocity grid, not by polygons.
The independent Sentinel-2 (HLS S30) check agrees on direction but gives about half the speed; HLS L30 agrees better but uses the same Landsat instruments.
No published migration rate exists for Sweihan, so there is nothing to compare against.
MERRA-2 wind is a ~0.5 x 0.625 deg reanalysis of hourly means; absolute drift potential is approximate and the regime is bimodal.

Farm targets are vegetated plots (HLS NDVI, last year) plus OSM farmland, which here includes the abandoned south-east farm grid and graded strips; built-up targets include large OSM landuse=residential zones, so a 'built-up area' hit can mean sand reaching the edge of zoned, partly empty land rather than buildings.

Results are valid for this box and 2013-2025 only; about {qc[masks][inbox_pct_nondune_total]:.0f} % of the box is masked as non-dune or changed ground (hand-drawn masks with reasons in pipeline/site_config/sweihan/), and nothing outside the box is assessed.
